verses.text: There was a man from the tribe of Benjamin named Kish, son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Bekorath, son of Aphiah. He was an important and wealthy man.
Kish had a son named Saul, a fine young man. No one in Israel was more handsome than he was, and he was a head taller than anyone else.
One day the donkeys belonging to Saul's father Kish got lost. So Kish said to his son Saul, "Take one of the servants with you and go and look for the donkeys."

So Saul went through the hill country of Ephraim and the area around Shalisha, but they did not find them. They went on into the area of Shaalim, but the donkeys were not there. Then he went through the land of Benjamin, but they still did not find them.
When they reached the area of Zuph, Saul said to the servant with him, "Come, let us go back home, or my father will stop thinking about the donkeys and start worrying about us."
But the servant replied, "Look, in this town there is a man of God. He is highly respected, and everything he says comes true. Let us go there now. Maybe he will tell us which way to go."
Saul said to his servant, "If we go, what can we give the man? The food in our bags is gone. We have no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?"
The servant answered him again. "Look," he said, "I have a quarter of a shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God so that he will tell us which way to go."
In the past in Israel, if someone went to ask God something, they would say, "Come, let us go to the seer," because the prophet of today used to be called a seer.
"Good," Saul said to his servant. "Come, let us go." So they set out for the town where the man of God lived.
As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and they asked them, "Is the seer here?"
"He is," they answered. "He is just ahead of you. Hurry, he has just come to our town today, because the people have a sacrifice at the place of worship on the hill.

As soon as you enter the town, you will find him before he goes up to the hill to eat. The people will not start eating until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice. After that, those who are invited will eat. Go up now. You should find him about this time."
So they went up to the town, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel, coming toward them on his way up to the place of worship.
The day before Saul came, the LORD had told Samuel,

"About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin. Anoint him as ruler over my people Israel. He will save my people from the Philistines. I have looked on my people, because their cry has reached me."
When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said to him, "This is the man I told you about. He will rule my people."
Saul came up to Samuel in the gateway and asked, "Please tell me where the seer's house is."
"I am the seer," Samuel replied. "Go up ahead of me to the place of worship, because today you are to eat with me. In the morning I will let you go and will tell you everything that is on your mind.
As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them. They have been found. And who is all Israel longing for? Is it not you and your father's whole family?"
Saul answered, "But I am from Benjamin, the smallest tribe of Israel, and my clan is the least important of all the clans of Benjamin. Why do you say such a thing to me?"
Then Samuel brought Saul and his servant into the hall and seated them at the head of the guests, about thirty people in all.
Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the piece of meat I gave you, the one I told you to set aside."

So the cook took up the thigh with what was on it and set it in front of Saul. Samuel said, "Here is what was kept for you. Eat, because it was set aside for you for this occasion, from the time I said, 'I have invited guests.'" And Saul ate with Samuel that day.
After they came down from the place of worship to the town, Samuel talked with Saul on the flat roof of his house.
They got up about daybreak, and Samuel called to Saul on the roof, "Get ready, and I will send you on your way." When Saul got ready, he and Samuel went outside together.

As they were going down to the edge of the town, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to go on ahead of us." The servant did so, and Samuel said, "But you stay here for a while, so that I may give you a message from God."
